questions.stem: A company runs a critical web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer in a single Availability Zone. The team wants to maximize availability with minimal application changes. What should a Solutions Architect recommend?

options.text: Deploy a NAT Gateway in front of the application.
options.reason: NAT Gateways provide outbound internet access for private subnets, not inbound high availability.

options.text: Place EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones and register them with the ALB.
Increase the size of the EC2 instances to handle more traffic.
options.reason: Vertical scaling improves capacity but does not eliminate the single-AZ failure domain.

options.text: Add Amazon CloudFront in front of the ALB.
options.reason: CloudFront improves latency and reduces origin load, but doesn't address the underlying single-AZ availability problem.

questions.stem: A workload runs continuously 24/7 for the next 3 years on EC2. Which pricing model offers the largest discount over On-Demand?

options.reason: Spot offers steep discounts but instances can be interrupted with two minutes' notice, which is unsuitable for steady 24/7 workloads.
On-Demand is the baseline price; it offers no discount.
Dedicated Hosts are more expensive than shared tenancy and meant for licensing/compliance, not cost savings.
